close_reason: round 1 complete: all P0/P1/P2 fixed; P3/P4 remainder carried to round 2
notes:
SEC2 efficiency review complete. One issue filed (PKIX-onc.1): TryFrom<Certificate> clones subject and SPKI fields it owns by value — 2 unnecessary heap allocations per construction. All other patterns are clean: find_cert_ext is O(n) over ≤10 extensions, nc_constrained_types init loop is O(P+E) and correct, NC seeding clones are semantically required (mutable walk state), intersection algorithm is O(P1*P2) but NC sets in real PKI are tiny (≤30 entries) and called at most chain_depth times.
SEC3 elegance: 4 real findings filed. (1) PKIX-onc.5: TryFrom<Certificate> calls .clone() on fields it owns — should be moves. (2) PKIX-onc.7: NC seeding initializes nc_permitted/nc_excluded via one tuple-destructuring match over two unrelated fields — two separate let bindings are clearer. (3) PKIX-onc.12: check_names closure uses require_match: bool boolean flag where false=excluded and true=permitted — a boolean trap; split into two named closures. (4) PKIX-onc.17: try_find_cert_ext name signals generic fallibility but not the fail-open vs fail-closed distinction that motivates the pair — rename or unify. No manufactured issues: TrustAnchor field ordering, #[non_exhaustive] placement, and nc_constrained_types init block are all clean.
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — six issues filed.
SEC4 readability review complete. 4 issues filed (PKIX-onc.8, .11, .14, .16). Passes: ANCHOR_NC_NOW constant is well-commented. Test names in anchor_nc.rs are self-explanatory. NC seeding block in chain_walk has RFC 6.1.2 citation. name_constraints field doc explains seeding. Issues: try_find_cert_ext missing doc contract, TryFrom missing fail-closed doc, TrustAnchor non_exhaustive missing rationale, find_cert_ext doc ambiguous 'this' referent.
SEC7 contradiction resolution: PKIX-onc.18 vs PKIX-onc.20 — PKIX-onc.20 (SEC0) is correct; PKIX-onc.18 (SEC6) is wrong. Code reading: check_names closure uses nc_constrained_types only in the require_match=true (permitted) branch (lines 1432-1435, 1446-1449). The require_match=false (excluded) branch never consults nc_constrained_types — it fires unconditionally on every name. Mid-chain excluded-subtrees update (lines 1371-1374) also does NOT set bits in nc_constrained_types; only permitted_subtrees entries do (lines 1302-1303). Therefore bits ORed into nc_constrained_types from anchor excluded entries are: (a) inconsistent with mid-chain excluded handling, and (b) serve no legitimate purpose since the excluded check never reads that bitmask. The false-positive scenario in PKIX-onc.20 is real: anchor with only excludedSubtrees=[dNSName:.evil.com] causes NC_TYPE_DNS bit to be set; when a later intermediate adds permittedSubtrees=[iPAddress:...], nc_permitted becomes Some([iPAddress:...]) and the permitted check fires for all constrained types including dNSName — but dNSName has no permitted entry, so every leaf with a dNSName SAN gets falsely rejected. PKIX-onc.18 should be closed as wrong; PKIX-onc.20 stands as a real P0 bug.
SEC7 duplicate: PKIX-onc.1, PKIX-onc.5, PKIX-onc.9 all describe the same clone-vs-move issue in TryFrom<Certificate>. Fix once, close all three.
SEC7 duplicate: PKIX-onc.4 (doc gap) and PKIX-onc.21 (RFC correctness violation) both address from_cert fail-open behavior. PKIX-onc.21 is the root cause — from_cert silently drops a critical NC extension without rejecting per RFC 5280 §4.2. PKIX-onc.4 is the consequence (missing doc warning). Fix PKIX-onc.21 first; PKIX-onc.4 may be resolved as part of it or separately.
Confidence: 85% chance of no missed bug beyond PKIX-onc.20 and PKIX-onc.21. Least confident flags: PKIX-onc.20 edge-case trigger — the false-positive only manifests when anchor has excluded-only NC and a later intermediate adds permitted entries of a different type; chains with no intermediate NC or with matching types are unaffected. Uncertainty driven by: (1) I cannot run the test suite to confirm the false-positive reproduces, (2) PKIX-onc.13 (seeding applied to intermediates not documented) needs verification that this is truly the anchor seeding path and not a different code path. Would raise confidence to 95% if: a targeted test demonstrating the PKIX-onc.20 false-positive was run and confirmed. The review is running out of real engineering complaints beyond PKIX-onc.20 and PKIX-onc.21. The remaining open P1s (PKIX-onc.1/5/9 deduped, PKIX-onc.4 as consequence of .21) are real but minor. P3/P4 findings are mostly opinion or pre-existing code outside PKIX-aoe scope.
